original_question: Is 1-almost-greediness equivalent to 1-semi-greediness for bases in Banach spaces, and also for bases in quasi-Banach spaces? In other words, when a basis attains the isometric constant 1 for almost-greedy approximation, must it also attain the constant 1 for semi-greedy approximation, and conversely?
target_in_paper: Question 4 in Section 4.1: Is it true that 1-almost-greediness is equivalent to 1-semi-greediness in the context of Banach (and quasi-Banach) spaces?
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper’s official open problem very closely. It correctly identifies the isometric constant-1 setting, asks for equivalence between 1-almost-greediness and 1-semi-greediness, includes both implication directions, and keeps the two ambient settings that the paper explicitly mentions: Banach spaces and quasi-Banach spaces.
missing_details: The paper poses this specifically as an isometric question about the exact constants C_al[B,X]=1 and C_sg[B,X]=1, not merely about qualitative almost-greedy versus semi-greedy equivalence.

The nearby definitions are given for semi-normalized Markushevich bases in quasi-Banach spaces; Schauder and bi-monotone hypotheses appear only in related partial results, so a stand-alone version should say what class of basis is being considered.
Almost-greediness is defined using projections onto finite greedy sets A of x: ||x-P_A(x)|| <= C inf_{|B|<=|A|} ||x-P_B(x)||. Your draft does not specify P_A or what a greedy set is.

Semi-greediness is defined via the best approximation supported on the same greedy set A: inf_{(a_n)_{n in A}} ||x-Σ_{n in A} a_n x_n|| <= C σ_|A|(x). Your draft does not spell out this Chebyshev-type minimization or the best m-term error σ_m(x).
The ambient scalar field in the paper is F = R or C.

The local context matters: the non-isometric equivalence is already known in Banach spaces for Markushevich bases and in quasi-Banach spaces for Schauder bases; the genuinely open point here is the constant-1 analogue.
refined_question: Let B=(x_n) be a semi-normalized Markushevich basis of a Banach space or quasi-Banach space X over F in {R,C}. For x in X and a finite greedy set A of x, let P_A(x)=Σ_{n in A} x_n^*(x)x_n, and let σ_m(x)=inf{||x-Σ_{n in B} b_n x_n|| : |B|<=m, b_n in F}. Is it true that C_al[B,X]=1 if and only if C_sg[B,X]=1, where C_al is the least constant C such that ||x-P_A(x)|| <= C inf_{|B|<=|A|} ||x-P_B(x)|| for every x in X and every finite greedy set A of x, and C_sg is the least constant C such that inf_{(a_n)_{n in A}} ||x-Σ_{n in A} a_n x_n|| <= C σ_|A|(x) for every x in X and every finite greedy set A of x? Equivalently, are 1-almost-greediness and 1-semi-greediness the same notion in the Banach-space and quasi-Banach-space settings considered in the paper?
justification: The draft clearly targets the paper’s official isometric open problem, which is stated verbatim as Question 4 in Section 4.1 (page 20). Definitions 4.8 and 4.14 provide the exact meanings of almost-greedy and semi-greedy, including the constants C_al and C_sg. Theorems 4.16 and 4.17 explain the already-known non-isometric equivalences in Banach and quasi-Banach settings, while Theorems 4.19 and 4.20 supply the immediate isometric context motivating the question. So the sharp paper-faithful refinement is to state the constant-1 equivalence using the exact projection and Chebyshev-error formulations attached to those definitions.
